newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel suggests simplification of tax structure.
newsitem.headline: India panel suggests simplification of tax structure.

text.p: A panel set up by the Indian government has recommended simplification of the domestic income tax rate structure, a government statement said on Wednesday.

In a report submitted to the government last month, the committee suggested the phasing out of a huge number of income tax exemptions and called for the streamlining of complex tax procedures, the statement said.
"The group has recommended lowering of tax rates for personal income tax as well as corporate tax," the statement said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram last week in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget included some of the recommendations in the tax proposals, it added.
Chidambaram slashed income and corporate taxes and import duties and offered a string of incentives to capital markets to boost economic growth.
The budget proposed to lower peak income tax rates for individuals to 30 percent from 40 percent.
It also proposed to cut corporate tax for domestic firms to 35 percent from 40 percent and for foreign firms to 48 percent from 55 percent.
The government proposes to present a new income tax bill in parliament taking into account the recommendations made by the panel.
"The government will take into account the reactions from all sections of the public before presenting the new bill," the statement said.
